en.title: There Is a Fountain Filled with Blood
en.author: William Cowper
stanzas:
[A]There is a foun[D]tain filled with [A]blood
Drawn from Im[E7]manuel's [A]veins;
And [A]sinners, plunged be[D]neath that [A]flood,
Lose [E7]all their guilty [A]stains:
[D]Lose all their guilty [A]stains,
[E7]Lose all their guilty [A]stains;
And [A]sinners, plunged be[D]neath that [A]flood,
Lose [E7]all their guilty [A]stains.

The dying thief rejoiced to see
That fountain in his day;
And there may I, though vile as he,
Wash all my sins away:
Wash all my sins away,
Wash all my sins away;
And there may I, though vile as he,
Wash all my sins away.

Dear dying Lamb, Thy precious blood
Shall never lose its pow'r,
Till all the ransomed Church of God
Be saved, to sin no more:
Be saved, to sin no more,
Be saved, to sin no more;
Till all the ransomed Church of God
Be saved to sin no more.

E'er since by faith I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die:
And shall be till I die,
And shall be till I die;
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.

When this poor lisping, stamm'ring tongue
Lies silent in the grave,
Then in a nobler, sweeter song
I'll sing Thy pow'r to save:
I'll sing Thy pow'r to save,
I'll sing Thy pow'r to save;
Then in a nobler, sweeter song
I'll sing Thy pow'r to save.

notes: Text is hymnary.org's representative text (Sing Joyfully, 1989), the five-stanza form sung to CLEANSING FOUNTAIN, whose repeated third/fourth lines are printed here as lines 5-8 of each stanza. The Cyber Hymnal (hymnary.org/hymn/CYBER/6556) prints Cowper's fuller original: it reads 'And there have I, though vile as he, washed all my sins away' in st. 2, reverses the couplets of st. 5 ('Then in a nobler, sweeter song' first), and adds a sixth stanza, 'Lord, I believe Thou hast prepared' — rarely printed today, so it is not shipped. Meter is as hymnary lists it for this text; the tune page gives the same tune as 8.6.8.6 D. Chords: hymnal key is B-flat Major, moved down a semitone to A per the guitar rule. Chart is a plain I-IV-V7 harmonization of the tune, not a transcription of a published arrangement. Independently checked against Timeless Truths (URL appended; tune, meter and B-flat key confirmed), which follows Cowper's original in st. 2 ('there have I ... Washed') and prints 'Are safe, to sin no more' where st. 3 here reads 'Be saved, to sin no more' — the shipped readings are the representative text's, kept.
